profile.headline: Staff Software Engineer at inRev
profile.summary:
I build the layer AI systems run on: identity, authorization, entitlements, and network policy. Most recently, the identity foundation for AI agents.
  
Five years on the platform team of an enterprise AI platform across AWS, Azure, GCP, on-prem, and 31 Kubernetes clusters. Created three production services, #1 contributor on five. Level 1 on-call: 16 incidents root-caused, 436 CVEs resolved.
  
Go, Python, TypeScript. OAuth/OIDC, Ory Hydra, Kubernetes, Cilium, OpenTelemetry.
  
On the side: Timbre (gettimbre.ai) and On the Tip (App Store).
  
Open to senior or staff roles in platform engineering, AI infrastructure, or identity for agentic systems.

Github: https://github.com/rembrandtreyes

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer, Access Services (Platform Engineering)
positions.description:
Identity, authorization, entitlements, and network policy for an enterprise AI platform (now the Agent Workforce Platform).
  
• Designed the identity foundation for AI agents: security-principal model, org-scoped RBAC, RFC 8693 delegation tokens. 
• Shipped external OAuth apps as security principals for an agent-to-agent MVP (private preview). 
• Per-org OAuth client auth on Ory Hydra: 500 req/s, zero 5xx, p99 12.3 ms. 
• Created a Go network-policy service (Cilium) and deployed it to 31 clusters; #1 contributor. 
• Level 1 on-call: 16 incidents root-caused, 5 postmortems, 436 CVEs resolved. • Cut p99 latency 35% and a CI build from 6 to 2 minutes; found $27–43K/yr in Kubernetes savings. 
• Onboarded a backend hire (a peer manager asked to replicate it); interviewer pool; 61 technical docs.

positions.title: Frontend Engineer II
positions.description: Core UI, then Customer Lifecycle Services. Authored the spec for and shipped social sign-up and sign-in (Google, GitHub) for the self-service trial through Auth0; built admin user-management improvements Customer Support called very useful; converted design-system components to TypeScript; wrote the team's frontend testing position paper.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
∆ Acquired by DataRobot
ML model deployment platform. Took the Cypress suites from half failing to fully passing; led the Webpack 4 → 5 upgrade clearing 5+ high CVEs; shipped org RBAC in the web client.

positions.title: UX/UI Engineer
positions.description:
• Owning features for hopjump.com from design, to development, to deployment.
• Work with product managers, and data analysts to build a platform that best suits our users
• Creating email templates to sustain our monthly revenue of $1 million dollars.
• Work with stakeholders to scope out new features and talk through acceptance criteria.
• Engage with my team in code reviews to ensure the highest standards are met within our codebase.

positions.title: Junior Developer
positions.description:
• Refactored hopjump.com code base to utilize TypeScript.
• Weekly website audits to find and squash bugs to improve our user experience and website performance.
• Researched user experiences to see how our customers interact with hopjump.com and making informed decisions to stakeholders on what we should prioritize for site improvements.

positions.title: Space Management Lead Analyst
positions.description:
• Provide leadership and support to a team of seven to manage four grocery categories.
• Create Space Automation scripts to help planogram analysts build planograms more efficiently.
• Working with planogram analysts to ascertain their database reporting needs.
• Take the database reporting needs and turn them into powerful SQL queries that will extract data and compile it into meaningful reports.
• Perform data loads and routine updates on an ongoing basis.
• Provide strategic insights and guidance to retail merchandising partners utilizing customer and competitive data to evaluate category performance to accomplish desired business goals.
• Integrate robust data analysis and variables to develop and maintain planograms reflecting the category’s strategic vision, most optimal assortments, merchandising guidelines and size requirements.
• Contribute to the continuous improvement and technological advancement efforts.
• Access relevant information, interpret results and provide in-depth and advanced interpretation of consumer behavior and category dynamics.
• Developing a comprehensive analysis of assigned merchandising categories.
• Creating and executing the most strategically successful planograms in the retail stores.
• Partnering with cross-functional teams to succeed together and support business objectives and goals.
• Collaborates with category teams to identify specific goals for the merchandise re-set to ensure approved criteria and best practices are followed and space allocation/shelf placement needs are met.
• Utilizing customer insights and competitive market data to execute on the team’s planogram goals.
• Pay close attention to timelines as the work is very deadline driven. 
• Initiating assortment recommendations and space allocation solutions which positively and measurably impact the Company’s sales and margins and turnover through proper assortment, shelf position, and allocation of all items.

projects.title: On the Tip (iOS)
projects.description: iPhone word game about the tip-of-the-tongue state: 150+ hand-written puzzles, progressive hints, a daily challenge, and streaks. Designed, built, and shipped solo to the App Store, September 2026. React Native / Expo, TypeScript.

projects.title: Timbre
projects.description: Live SaaS that learns a writer's voice and rewrites one draft into platform-native posts for LinkedIn, X, Threads, Medium, and Substack. Paid tiers. Designed, built, and shipped solo: Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase (PostgreSQL), OpenAI API.
